label: D2 rare a1->S2 transition (strongly up), a2->S1 down
terms: (phase == D2) * (action == 1) * (state == S2) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 2) * (state == S1) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 1) * (state == S1) ;; (phase == D2) * (prev_action == 1) ;; (phase == D2) * (prev_reward == 0) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 2) * (state == S2) * (prev_reward == 0) ;; (phase != D2) * (prev_action == 1) * (1 - prev_reward)
explanation: Raw candidate n of unit 25 sits near -0.97 at D1/GO and about -0.6 at D2, rising late in the episode (timing R^2 0.46). Beyond timing, it is almost entirely a D2 code of the just-made choice x reached state: a1 reaching S2 (rare) raises it strongly (+0.79), a2 reaching S1 (rare) lowers it (-0.44), a1 reaching S1 (common) lowers it modestly (-0.23), a2->S2 is the reference. These three D2 terms alone give dev R^2 beyond timing 0.74. Smaller D2 modulations: higher when the previous trial chose a1 (+0.14) and when the previous trial was unrewarded (+0.07, extra +0.14 for a2->S2 after no reward). At D1/GO there is only a small rise (+0.09) after an unrewarded a1 trial. All terms are observed at their step (no future variables); value and the trial-before reward add little. Test R^2 beyond timing 0.80 vs all-cue ceiling 0.92.

issues: The factual claims hold. On the test split the 7 terms give R^2 beyond timing 0.7986. Fitted weights: a1->S2 +0.79, a2->S1 -0.44, a1->S1 -0.23, D2 prev a1 +0.14, D2 prev unrewarded +0.07, a2->S2 after no reward +0.14, D1/GO after unrewarded a1 +0.085. The profile residuals by this choice x state at D2 agree: a1S1 -0.13, a1S2 +0.90, a2S1 -0.43, a2S2 -0.01. D1/GO effects are small (at most +0.088, after a1 S2 u). The late-episode rise comes from timing, not from any term.

A large systematic error class remains: the spread within the common a2->S2 cell at D2. The worst-fit windows are almost all a2->S2c steps after runs of unrewarded trials. Actual values are +0.29 to +0.80; predicted are -0.06 to -0.28. The terms only model the previous reward, and these values reach the scale of the claimed 'strongly up' rare effect. Misses also over-predict D2 after a1 S2 r (-0.187), and after a2 S2 r and a2 S1 u (both -0.103).

The D2 magnitude also follows the agent's policy logit at D2 (profile policy-decile residual at D2 runs from -0.44 to +0.58). Adding one term, (phase==D2)*choice, raises test R^2 beyond timing from 0.799 to 0.880. With that term the a2->S1 weight shrinks from -0.44 to -0.16 and the a2->S2-after-no-reward weight grows from +0.14 to +0.33. So the label's 'a2->S1 down' is largely shared with the policy (a2 preference), not a pure transition effect.

Observed-only history proxies recover only part of this. Counts of unrewarded / rewarded past S2 visits inside a2->S2 give 0.821. Signed state-reward history over 3 trials gives 0.762. The 'all observed' reference is only 0.82, so the remaining gap up to 0.92 sits mainly in model-output cues (policy), which the explanation never mentions.

The label 'rare a1->S2 transition (strongly up), a2->S1 down' leaves out that the unit's D2 value also scales with the agent's current a1-vs-a2 preference, and that a2->S2 rises a lot after unrewarded streaks.
skeptic.revised_label: D2 choice x state code (a1->S2 rare strongly up, a1->S1 / a2->S1 down) plus the agent's a1 preference at D2; a2->S2 rises after unrewarded trials
